subject.title: fix: Windows /restart falls back to in-process restart without changing PID

question: Should an env-less Windows gateway with an installed Scheduled Task be treated as supervised by probing Task Scheduler, and must that probe resolve the same default/profile/custom task name used by the restart handoff?
rationale: This is a real bug path, but the safe permanent behavior affects Windows restart fallback semantics and can break availability if a false-positive task causes the current gateway to exit before the intended replacement is available.

options.title: Use exact-task schtasks detection
options.body: Require the linked PR or replacement to probe the same default/profile/custom task name used by the handoff and include redacted Windows `/restart` plus `/status` proof.

options.title: Keep env-only supervision
options.body: Leave manually started env-less Windows gateways on the in-process fallback and document that full PID-changing restart requires starting through the Scheduled Task.

options.title: Fold into broader restart recovery
options.body: Defer this path to the broader Windows schtasks restart reliability work so detection, failed `/Run`, status half-states, and fallback behavior are decided together.

recommendation.title: Use exact-task schtasks detection
recommendation.body: Require the linked PR or replacement to probe the same default/profile/custom task name used by the handoff and include redacted Windows `/restart` plus `/status` proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Windows restart handoff work makes this the best current routing candidate, with obviyus and mjamiv as important history owners.
